newsitem.title: USA: Motorola to phase out DRAM production by mid-2000.
newsitem.headline: Motorola to phase out DRAM production by mid-2000.

text.p: Motorola Inc. said Tuesday it plans to stop making dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips and will phase out production in stages by mid-2000.
In the first stage, Motorola expects to end 16-megabit DRAM production at a Japanese joint-venture plant with Toshiba Corp. by the end of this year, a spokesman said.

As a result of the phase-out, Motorola said it will take a second-quarter pretax charge of $170 million. It declined to give any guidance on second-quarter earnings, which are expected to be released July 8, but said the charges relate to the write-down of both technology development costs and manufacturing equipment.

Motorola said it has had limited participation of less than 5 percent in the DRAM market since the mid-1980s. During the past three years, its share of the market has been less than 2 percent, it said.

Ken Phillips, a company spokesman, said Motorola was moving out of DRAM to focus on faster memory products used in higher-speed computers, such as flash static random access memory products, or FSRAM, and electrically erasable programmable read-only memory, or EEPROM.
Motorola's production of 64-megabit DRAM at a Siemens AG joint venture plant now under construction in Virginia is expected to end in mid-2000.
While the new generations of higher speed computers also use DRAMs, this market is more competitive and fragmented with suppliers, Phillips said.
Motorola declined to comment on the current financial conditions of its DRAM business. A spokesman did say that the DRAM segment was not profitable in 1996.
The electronics and technology giant plans to shift its share of output at the Toshiba venture into local products for computers.
Phillips said the shift out of DRAMs into other computer memory and logic products reflects Motorola's strategy to organise its businesses based on market focus as opposed to product groups.
Motorola provides wireless communications, semiconductors, and advanced electronic systems, components, and services. Its stock was up $1 at $77 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
